newsitem.title: USA: Ohio judge abandons fight against false-ad verdict.
newsitem.headline: Ohio judge abandons fight against false-ad verdict.

text.p: A veteran appeals court judge faced possible suspension for using false campaign advertisements after his withdrawal Wednesday of an appeal of a judgment against him by the Ohio Supreme Court.
The supreme court, in Columbus, accepted Judge Lee Hildebrandt's withdrawal of his appeal and reinstated the $15,000 fine and possible six-month suspension from the bench that it imposed in February.

Former U.S. Representative David S. Mann, Hildebrandt's Democratic opponent, had accused the Republican incumbent of misrepresenting Mann's position on the death penalty when he ran for Hildebrandt's seat on the Ohio 1st District Court of Appeals last November.
He said Hildebrandt's television ad blitz portrayed him as voting against capital punishment as a congressman when, in fact, he had supported the death penalty.
Mann said political polls showed that the false ads cost him the election.

The Ohio Supreme Court, acting on the recommendation of its Commission of Judges, ordered Hildebrandt to issue a public apology to Mann in the local news media or face a six-month suspension without pay from the bench.

Hildebrandt was unavailable Wednesday to say what he would do, and his attorneys declined to speak in his behalf. Hildebrandt had maintained in his appeal that the ads did not misrepresent Mann's position.

Mann's attorney and brother-in-law, Phil Taliaferro, said: "Dave feels he has been fully vindicated. But we're still a little disappointed that the court did not kick Hildebrandt out of office. That's the penalty we had sought."
